close_reason: Already defended: src/methods/event_notification.rs:74-105 rationale block + README + PLAN.md document the destroy-only design. Section-6 'good-decision' note, no code change required.
description:
src/methods/event_notification.rs:80-113 deliberately exposes ONLY a `destroy` parameter — no create or update. The doc-comment, README §5, and PLAN.md all explain why: draft §7.3 mandates the server reject create/update with `forbidden`, so accepting them in the client API would let callers construct guaranteed-failing requests.

A contributor might 'normalize' this method to match calendar_event_set's three-arg signature for consistency. DO NOT. The asymmetry is load-bearing — it's a type-system encoding of a spec invariant. The right way to 'fix' this if it ever becomes a problem is to remove the method entirely and require the caller to use a destroy-only API on a generic set helper.
title: calendar_event_notification_set is destroy-only, not 'set with all-Forbidden errors'
